name: PM-KISAN (Pradhan Mantri Kisan Samman Nidhi)
target_group: Landholding farmer families
description: Direct income support to landholding farmer families for farm and household needs.
benefits: ₹6,000 per year in three instalments of ₹2,000, paid directly to the bank account.
notes: Cultivable land ownership is required. Institutional landholders, income-tax payers and some government employees or pensioners are excluded.
how_to_apply: Register on the PM-KISAN portal or at a Common Service Centre and complete e-KYC.

name: PM Fasal Bima Yojana (Crop Insurance)
target_group: Farmers growing notified crops
description: Crop insurance that protects farmers against crop loss from natural calamities, pests and diseases.
benefits: Insurance cover for crop loss at a low farmer-paid premium (2% for kharif, 1.5% for rabi, 5% for commercial/horticultural crops).
notes: Crop must be notified in your area for that season.
how_to_apply: Apply through your bank, a Common Service Centre or the PMFBY portal before the cut-off date for the season.

name: Kisan Credit Card (KCC)
ministry: Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare / Banks
target_group: Farmers, tenant farmers and allied-activity farmers
description: Easy short-term credit for cultivation, farm expenses and allied activities like dairy and fisheries.
benefits: Short-term farm credit with interest subvention on timely repayment.
notes: Limits and interest benefits depend on the bank and current government guidelines.
how_to_apply: Apply at your bank branch or cooperative bank.

name: Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY
target_group: Economically vulnerable families and senior citizens aged 70+
description: Cashless hospital treatment cover for secondary and tertiary care at empanelled hospitals.
benefits: Health cover up to ₹5 lakh per family per year for hospitalisation.
notes: Eligibility is based on SECC deprivation and occupational criteria, and senior citizens aged 70 and above are covered under the expanded scheme. Check your name on the official portal.
how_to_apply: Check eligibility on the PM-JAY portal and get your Ayushman card at a Common Service Centre or empanelled hospital.

name: PM Awas Yojana – Gramin
target_group: Rural households without a pucca house
description: Financial assistance to build a pucca house with basic amenities.
benefits: Assistance of ₹1.20 lakh in plain areas and ₹1.30 lakh in hilly or difficult areas.
notes: Beneficiaries are selected from the SECC / Awaas+ lists. Households that already own a pucca house are not eligible.
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat or block office to confirm your name in the beneficiary list.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for SC Students
target_group: Scheduled Caste students in post-matriculation courses
description: Financial assistance for higher education to SC students from low-income families.
benefits: Fee reimbursement plus a maintenance allowance for the course duration.
notes: Parental income ceiling applies. Check the latest limit on the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: Central Sector Scholarship for College & University Students
target_group: Meritorious students from low-income families in higher education
description: Merit-based scholarship for students above the 80th percentile in Class 12 who pursue regular degree courses.
benefits: Annual scholarship to help with college and living expenses (check current amounts on the portal).
notes: Requires a Class 12 percentile above the cut-off and a regular course at a recognised institution.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal.

name: Sukanya Samriddhi Yojana
target_group: Parents or guardians of a girl child below 10 years
description: A small-savings account for a girl child's future education and marriage expenses.
benefits: Government-notified interest rate and tax benefits on the savings.
notes: The account is opened in the name of a girl child below 10 years by her parent or legal guardian.
how_to_apply: Open the account at a post office or authorised bank.

name: Atal Pension Yojana
target_group: Unorganised-sector workers aged 18–40
description: A pension scheme that gives a guaranteed monthly pension after age 60.
benefits: Guaranteed monthly pension of ₹1,000 to ₹5,000 after age 60, depending on contribution.
notes: Income-tax payers cannot join. A savings bank or post office account is required.
how_to_apply: Apply through your bank or post office.

name: PM Jeevan Jyoti Bima Yojana
target_group: Bank account holders aged 18–50
description: Low-cost life insurance with auto-debit of the yearly premium.
benefits: ₹2 lakh life cover for death from any cause, with a premium of roughly ₹436 per year.
notes: Requires a bank account with auto-debit consent. Cover continues up to age 55.
how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank branch or net banking.

name: PM Suraksha Bima Yojana
target_group: Bank account holders aged 18–70
description: Accidental death and disability insurance at a very low annual premium.
benefits: ₹2 lakh cover for accidental death or full disability, with a premium of roughly ₹20 per year.
notes: Requires a bank account with auto-debit consent.
how_to_apply: Enrol through your bank branch or net banking.

name: PM MUDRA Yojana
target_group: Micro and small non-farm business owners and entrepreneurs
description: Collateral-free loans to start or grow small businesses in manufacturing, trading and services.
benefits: Loans up to ₹10 lakh under the Shishu, Kishor and Tarun categories.
notes: Applies to non-corporate, non-farm income-generating activities.
how_to_apply: Apply at a bank, NBFC or micro-finance institution, or via the Udyamimitra portal.

name: Stand-Up India
target_group: SC/ST and/or women entrepreneurs starting a new enterprise
description: Bank loans to help SC/ST and women entrepreneurs set up new (greenfield) businesses.
benefits: Bank loans between ₹10 lakh and ₹1 crore for manufacturing, services or trading.
notes: Applicant must be SC/ST and/or a woman, and the enterprise must be new. Must not be a defaulter to any bank.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Stand-Up Mitra portal or at a bank branch.

name: PM SVANidhi (Street Vendors)
target_group: Street vendors in urban areas
description: Affordable working-capital loans for street vendors with incentives for digital payments.
benefits: Collateral-free working-capital loans in increasing tranches, with an interest subsidy on timely repayment.
notes: Vendors usually need a certificate of vending or letter of recommendation from the urban local body.
how_to_apply: Apply on the PM SVANidhi portal or through a Common Service Centre.

name: PM Vishwakarma
target_group: Traditional artisans and craftspeople
description: Recognition, skill training, toolkits and low-cost credit for artisans in traditional trades.
benefits: PM Vishwakarma certificate and ID, training with a ₹500/day stipend, ₹15,000 toolkit incentive, and collateral-free credit up to ₹3 lakh.
notes: Covers 18 listed traditional trades. Applicants must work with hands and tools and not be salaried government employees.
how_to_apply: Register at a Common Service Centre or on the PM Vishwakarma portal.

name: PM Kaushal Vikas Yojana (PMKVY)
target_group: Unemployed youth and school or college dropouts
description: Free short-term skill training with certification to improve job prospects.
benefits: Free skill training, a recognised certificate and placement support.
notes: Open to Indian nationals. Course availability varies by training centre.
how_to_apply: Find a training centre on the Skill India portal and register.

name: MGNREGA
target_group: Adult members of rural households willing to do unskilled manual work
description: A legal guarantee of wage employment for rural households.
benefits: Up to 100 days of guaranteed wage employment per rural household per financial year.
notes: A job card issued by the Gram Panchayat is required.
how_to_apply: Apply to your Gram Panchayat for a job card, then request work.

name: Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme
target_group: Senior citizens aged 60+ from below-poverty-line households
description: A monthly pension for elderly people from poor households.
benefits: Monthly old-age pension (central amount, often topped up by the state).
notes: Applicant must belong to a BPL household. Pension amount varies by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Gram Panchayat, municipality or state social welfare department.

name: PM Ujjwala Yojana
target_group: Adult women from poor households without an LPG connection
description: LPG connections for poor households to promote clean cooking fuel.
benefits: Deposit-free LPG connection in the woman's name.
notes: The household must not already have an LPG connection and must meet the poverty criteria.
how_to_apply: Apply at a nearby LPG distributor or on the PMUY portal.

name: PM Matru Vandana Yojana
target_group: Pregnant and lactating women (first living child)
description: Cash incentive to support nutrition and partly compensate wage loss during pregnancy and after childbirth.
benefits: ₹5,000 in instalments for the first living child (extra support may apply for a second girl child).
notes: Regular central or state government employees are usually excluded as they get maternity benefits.
how_to_apply: Register at your nearest Anganwadi Centre or health facility.

name: PM Awas Yojana – Urban 2.0
target_group: Urban families (EWS, LIG, MIG) without a pucca house
description: Support for urban families to build, buy or rent an affordable home.
benefits: Central assistance for building or buying a house, or an interest subsidy on a home loan.
notes: The family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India. Income groups are EWS, LIG and MIG, and the limits can change, so check the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply on the PMAY-Urban portal or through your Urban Local Body.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for ST Students
target_group: Scheduled Tribe students in post-matriculation courses
description: Financial help for ST students from low-income families to continue higher education.
benefits: Fee reimbursement plus a maintenance allowance for the course duration.
notes: Parental income ceiling applies. Check the latest limit on the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: PM YASASVI Scholarship (OBC / EBC / DNT)
target_group: OBC, EBC and DNT students from low-income families
description: Scholarships to support school and college education for OBC, EBC and denotified tribe students.
benefits: Scholarship support for studies (amount depends on the class or course).
notes: Also covers EBC and DNT students. Income limit and scholarship amounts can change, so verify on the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the National Scholarship Portal.

name: National Means-cum-Merit Scholarship (NMMSS)
target_group: Talented Class 8 students from low-income families
description: A scholarship that helps bright students from poor families continue school from Class 9 to 12.
benefits: ₹12,000 per year for Classes 9 to 12.
notes: Students are selected through a state-level selection test and must study in government or aided schools. Minimum marks in Class 7 apply.
how_to_apply: Apply through your school and the National Scholarship Portal after clearing the state selection test.

name: PM POSHAN (Mid-Day Meal)
target_group: Children studying in government and aided schools (Classes 1–8)
description: A hot cooked meal on school days to improve nutrition and school attendance.
benefits: One free hot cooked meal on every school day.
notes: Available automatically to enrolled children in government and government-aided schools. No separate application is usually needed.
how_to_apply: Enrol in a government or aided school. The school provides the meal.

name: PM Jan Dhan Yojana
target_group: Anyone without a bank account
description: Zero-balance bank accounts that bring every household into the banking system.
benefits: Zero-balance savings account, RuPay debit card with accident insurance cover, and an overdraft facility.
notes: Aimed at people who do not yet have a bank account. Overdraft and insurance terms apply as per the latest rules.
how_to_apply: Visit any bank branch or Bank Mitra and ask for a Jan Dhan account.

name: PM Shram Yogi Maan-dhan (PM-SYM)
target_group: Unorganised-sector workers aged 18–40
description: A voluntary pension scheme for unorganised workers such as labourers, vendors and artisans.
benefits: Assured monthly pension of ₹3,000 after age 60, with the government matching your contribution.
notes: Monthly income must be ₹15,000 or less. You must not be a member of EPFO, ESIC or NPS, and must not pay income tax.
documents: Savings bank account or Jan Dhan account
how_to_apply: Enrol at a Common Service Centre with your Aadhaar and bank details.

name: PM Kisan Maan-dhan Yojana
target_group: Small and marginal farmers aged 18–40
description: A voluntary pension scheme for small and marginal farmers.
benefits: Assured monthly pension of ₹3,000 after age 60.
notes: For small and marginal farmers (up to about 2 hectares). Those covered by other pension schemes or paying income tax are excluded.
how_to_apply: Enrol at a Common Service Centre.

name: National Food Security Act – Ration Card
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
target_group: Priority and Antyodaya households
description: Free foodgrains every month to eligible households through the public distribution system.
benefits: Free foodgrains every month through your ration shop (quantity depends on the ration card category).
notes: Eligibility is decided by your state government and the type of ration card you hold.
how_to_apply: Apply for a ration card on your state food and civil supplies portal or at the local food office.

name: DAY-NRLM (Self-Help Groups for Rural Women)
target_group: Rural women from poor households
description: Helps rural women form self-help groups, access cheap credit and build livelihoods.
benefits: Support to form self-help groups, bank credit at low interest, training and livelihood support.
notes: Run through State Rural Livelihood Missions. Join an existing self-help group or form a new one.
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat or block office to join or form a self-help group.

name: PM Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP)
target_group: Individuals starting a new micro-enterprise
description: A credit-linked subsidy for setting up new self-employment ventures.
benefits: Margin-money subsidy of roughly 15–35% of the project cost (higher for special categories and rural areas). Maximum project cost ₹50 lakh for manufacturing and ₹20 lakh for services.
notes: Only for new projects. Educational qualification rules apply for larger projects. Subsidy percentages vary by category and location.
how_to_apply: Apply online on the PMEGP e-portal, then your application goes to a bank for the loan.

name: PM-KUSUM (Solar Pumps for Farmers)
target_group: Farmers who need irrigation pumps
description: Subsidy to install solar irrigation pumps or solarise existing pumps.
benefits: Subsidy on solar pumps from the central and state governments, cutting electricity and diesel costs.
notes: Run by state nodal agencies, so subsidy levels and availability vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state nodal agency or the PM-KUSUM state portal.

name: Soil Health Card Scheme
target_group: All farmers
description: Free soil testing with crop-wise recommendations on fertiliser use.
benefits: A free soil health card with nutrient status and fertiliser advice for your land.
notes: Soil samples are collected on a periodic cycle by the state agriculture department.
how_to_apply: Contact your local agriculture office or register on the Soil Health Card portal.

name: Agriculture Infrastructure Fund
target_group: Farmers, FPOs, agri-entrepreneurs and start-ups
description: Medium and long-term loans for post-harvest and farm infrastructure like warehouses and cold storage.
benefits: Loans with interest subvention (about 3% on loans up to ₹2 crore) and credit guarantee support.
notes: For post-harvest management and community farming assets. Terms are set by the latest scheme guidelines.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Agriculture Infrastructure Fund portal and through a participating bank.

name: PM Internship Scheme
target_group: Youth aged 21–24 not in full-time education or employment
description: A 12-month paid internship with top companies to gain real work experience.
benefits: Monthly internship stipend of about ₹5,000 plus a one-time assistance amount.
notes: Family income limit applies, and no family member should hold a government job. This scheme has been running in phases, so check whether applications are currently open.
how_to_apply: Register and apply on the PM Internship portal.

name: DDU-GKY (Rural Skills & Placement)
target_group: Rural youth from poor families
description: Free skill training linked to jobs for rural youth.
benefits: Free residential or non-residential skill training, with placement support.
notes: General candidates are usually aged 15–35, with relaxation up to 45 for women, SC/ST and some other groups. Check the training partner's criteria.
how_to_apply: Register on the DDU-GKY portal or at a nearby training centre.

name: Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY)
target_group: Pregnant women delivering in a government or accredited health facility
description: Cash support to encourage safe institutional delivery.
benefits: Cash assistance for delivery in a government or accredited facility.
notes: Eligibility conditions and amounts differ by state and between rural and urban areas.
how_to_apply: Register at your ASHA worker, Anganwadi or nearest government health centre.

name: Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)
target_group: Pregnant women and sick newborns in government health facilities
description: Free and cashless services for mothers and newborns at public hospitals.
benefits: Free delivery including C-section, medicines, tests, diet, blood and transport for mothers and sick infants.
notes: Available at government health facilities. Entitlements may vary slightly by state.
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest government hospital or ask your ASHA worker.

name: PM Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan (PMSMA)
target_group: Pregnant women
description: Free antenatal check-ups by doctors to find and manage high-risk pregnancies.
benefits: Free check-ups, tests and advice on the 9th of every month at government facilities.
notes: Visit a government health centre on the 9th of each month.
how_to_apply: Go to a nearby government health facility on the 9th of any month.

name: Senior Citizen Savings Scheme (SCSS)
target_group: Senior citizens aged 60+
description: A safe savings scheme for retirees with regular interest income.
benefits: Government-set interest paid every quarter, with tax benefits on deposits (up to the current maximum deposit limit).
notes: Retirees aged 55–60 can join under certain conditions. Interest rate and maximum deposit are set by the government and can change.
how_to_apply: Open an account at a post office or authorised bank.

name: Public Provident Fund (PPF)
target_group: Any resident individual
description: A long-term savings scheme with government-set interest and tax benefits.
benefits: 15-year savings with government-set interest rate and tax benefits.
notes: Annual deposit limits apply. Interest rate is revised by the government every quarter.
how_to_apply: Open a PPF account at a post office or authorised bank.

name: Ayushman Vay Vandana Card (70+)
target_group: Senior citizens aged 70 and above
description: Health insurance for all senior citizens aged 70+ under Ayushman Bharat.
benefits: Health cover up to ₹5 lakh per year for hospital treatment.
notes: Open to all citizens aged 70 and above, regardless of income. Details of top-up cover may differ if you already have other government health insurance.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Ayushman Bharat portal or app, or at an empanelled hospital.

name: PM Bharatiya Janaushadhi Pariyojana
target_group: Everyone, especially families with regular medicine expenses
description: Quality generic medicines at much lower prices through Jan Aushadhi Kendras.
benefits: Generic medicines at prices far below branded medicines.
notes: No application needed. Buy from any Jan Aushadhi Kendra with a prescription.
how_to_apply: Find your nearest Jan Aushadhi Kendra using the official locator.

name: Swachh Bharat Mission – Gramin (Household Toilet)
target_group: Eligible rural households without a toilet
description: Incentive to build a household toilet in rural areas.
benefits: Financial incentive of ₹12,000 for building an individual household toilet.
notes: Usually for BPL, SC/ST, small and marginal farmers, landless labourers with a homestead, and women-headed households. Rules may vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Gram Panchayat or the SBM-G portal.

name: PM Surya Ghar Muft Bijli Yojana
target_group: Households with a valid electricity connection and a suitable roof
description: Subsidy for installing rooftop solar panels at home to cut electricity bills.
benefits: Central subsidy on rooftop solar (up to ₹78,000 for larger systems) and lower or zero electricity bills.
notes: You need your own house with a roof suitable for solar and a valid electricity connection. Subsidy depends on system capacity.
how_to_apply: Register on the PM Surya Ghar portal and choose an empanelled vendor.

name: Startup India Recognition
ministry: Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)
target_group: Innovative start-ups
description: Official recognition that unlocks tax benefits, easier compliance and funding access for start-ups.
benefits: DPIIT recognition, possible tax exemption, easier compliance and access to funding schemes.
notes: The entity must be a private limited company, LLP or partnership firm, working on innovation, and within the age and turnover limits.
how_to_apply: Register and apply for recognition on the Startup India portal.

name: AICTE Pragati Scholarship for Girls
target_group: Girl students in AICTE-approved technical degree or diploma courses
description: Scholarship for girls to pursue technical education.
benefits: Annual scholarship amount for tuition and other expenses (check the current amount on the portal).
notes: Usually limited to two girl children per family and to admission in AICTE-approved institutions.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: PM Vidyalaxmi (Education Loan Support)
target_group: Students admitted to top-ranked higher-education institutions
description: Collateral-free, guarantee-backed education loans for meritorious students.
benefits: Education loans without collateral, with interest subvention for students from families under the income limit.
notes: For admission to eligible institutions. Interest subvention applies to families under the income limit, so check the latest rules.
how_to_apply: Apply through the PM Vidyalaxmi portal, which sends your application to participating banks.

name: PM Special Scholarship Scheme for J&K and Ladakh (PMSSS)
target_group: Students from Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh studying outside the UT
description: Scholarship for J&K and Ladakh students who study at institutions in other states.
benefits: Tuition fee support and an academic and maintenance allowance.
notes: Requires a domicile of J&K or Ladakh and admission to a participating institution outside the UT. Check the current academic year's notice.
how_to_apply: Register on the PMSSS portal during the application window and take part in counselling.

name: Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme
target_group: Widows aged 40–79 from below-poverty-line households
description: A monthly pension for widows from poor households.
benefits: Monthly widow pension (central amount, often topped up by the state).
notes: The applicant must be a widow in a BPL household. Pension amounts vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Gram Panchayat, municipality or state social welfare department.

name: PM Matsya Sampada Yojana (Fisheries)
ministry: Ministry of Fisheries, Animal Husbandry & Dairying
target_group: Fishers, fish farmers, fish workers and fisheries entrepreneurs
description: Support to grow fisheries, aquaculture and related livelihoods.
benefits: Subsidy on fisheries projects (about 40% for general beneficiaries and 60% for SC/ST and women), plus support for fishing assets and training.
notes: Project-based. Eligible activities and subsidy depend on the component and your state fisheries department.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state fisheries department or the PMMSY portal.

name: PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME)
target_group: Micro food-processing units, FPOs and self-help groups
description: Support for small food-processing businesses to upgrade, formalise and grow.
benefits: Credit-linked subsidy of 35% of project cost up to ₹10 lakh per unit, plus training and branding support.
notes: For existing micro food-processing units, with some support for new group-based units. Check the scheme guidelines for the latest terms.
how_to_apply: Apply on the PMFME portal or through your State Nodal Agency.

name: National Apprenticeship Training Scheme (NATS)
target_group: Graduates, diploma holders and technical students seeking apprenticeships
description: On-the-job apprenticeship training with a stipend, linking young people to employers.
benefits: Hands-on apprenticeship with a monthly stipend, where the government shares part of the stipend cost with the employer.
notes: Stipend share and rules are set by the current guidelines, so verify on the portal.
how_to_apply: Register on the NATS portal and apply to listed apprenticeship opportunities.

name: Saksham Scholarship (AICTE) for Differently-Abled Students
target_group: Students with benchmark disability in AICTE-approved technical courses
description: Scholarship for differently-abled students pursuing technical degree or diploma courses.
benefits: Annual scholarship towards tuition and other expenses (check the current amount on the portal).
notes: Needs a disability certificate (40% or more) and admission to an AICTE-approved institution.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: Post Matric Scholarship for Minorities
target_group: Students from notified minority communities after Class 10
description: Financial help for minority students from low-income families to continue higher studies.
benefits: Admission and tuition fee support plus a maintenance allowance.
notes: For Muslim, Christian, Sikh, Buddhist, Jain and Parsi students. A minimum of 50% marks in the previous exam is usually required.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: Merit-cum-Means Scholarship for Minorities
target_group: Minority students in professional and technical courses
description: Scholarship for meritorious minority students from low-income families in professional courses.
benefits: Course fee support and a maintenance allowance.
notes: Requires at least 50% marks in the qualifying exam and admission to a technical or professional course.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal during the open window.

name: INSPIRE Scholarship for Higher Education (SHE)
target_group: Top-performing students taking up natural and basic sciences
description: Scholarship that encourages bright students to study basic sciences at BSc and Integrated MSc level.
benefits: Annual scholarship of about ₹80,000 plus a summer research attachment (verify current amounts).
notes: Open to students in the top percentile of Class 12 boards or top ranks in national entrance exams, studying natural or basic sciences.
how_to_apply: Apply on the INSPIRE-MANAK / DST INSPIRE portal when applications open.

name: Interest Subsidy on Education Loans (CSIS)
target_group: Students from low-income families taking bank education loans
description: Government pays the interest on your education loan during the course and a short period after.
benefits: Interest subsidy during the course period plus the moratorium (up to one year after the course).
notes: For approved professional and technical courses in India. Terms are updated through the PM Vidyalaxmi framework.
how_to_apply: Apply through your bank or the PM Vidyalaxmi portal.

name: SWAYAM (Free Online Courses)
target_group: Anyone who wants free online courses, from school to postgraduate level
description: A national platform with free courses from top Indian institutions.
benefits: Free courses and study material, with an optional paid proctored exam for a certificate.
notes: Credit transfer depends on whether your institution accepts the course.
how_to_apply: Create a free account on the SWAYAM portal and enrol in a course.

name: Scholarship for Top Class Education for SC Students
target_group: SC students admitted to notified top institutions
description: Full financial support for SC students studying at top-ranked colleges and universities.
benefits: Tuition fee and non-refundable charges, plus living expenses and an allowance for books and a computer.
notes: Only for courses at institutions on the notified list. Check the latest income ceiling on the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal.

name: Pre-Matric Scholarship for SC Students (Class 9–10)
target_group: SC students in Classes 9 and 10
description: Scholarship for SC school students from low-income families to reduce dropouts.
benefits: Annual scholarship amount plus an ad-hoc grant for school needs.
notes: Parental income ceiling applies. Check the latest limit and amounts on the portal.
how_to_apply: Apply on the National Scholarship Portal through your school.

name: Kasturba Gandhi Balika Vidyalaya (KGBV)
target_group: Girls from SC, ST, OBC, minority and BPL families
description: Free residential schools for girls from disadvantaged groups in educationally backward areas.
benefits: Free residential schooling with food, books and uniform.
notes: Run in selected backward blocks. Admission is through the local education office.
how_to_apply: Contact your block education office or the nearest KGBV for admission.

name: Eklavya Model Residential Schools (EMRS)
target_group: Scheduled Tribe students in Classes 6 to 12
description: Free quality residential schools for tribal children.
benefits: Free education with boarding, lodging, books and uniforms.
notes: Admission is through an entrance test, with seats reserved for ST students.
how_to_apply: Apply during the annual EMRS admission notice through the official portal.

name: Khelo India Athlete Scheme
target_group: Talented young athletes identified through national competitions
description: Long-term financial support for promising athletes.
benefits: Annual support for coaching, equipment and living costs (about ₹6.28 lakh per athlete per year; verify the current amount).
notes: Athletes are selected from Khelo India Games and other national events, not by open application.
how_to_apply: Take part in Khelo India and national events, and check the Sports Authority of India notices.

name: Prime Minister's Research Fellowship (PMRF)
target_group: Outstanding students pursuing PhD at IITs, IISc, IISERs and NITs
description: A fellowship that attracts the best talent into doctoral research.
benefits: Monthly fellowship (roughly ₹70,000–80,000) plus an annual research grant (verify current amounts).
notes: Selection is through a national process with a minimum CGPA and GATE or equivalent score.
how_to_apply: Apply on the PMRF portal when the call opens.

name: Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)
target_group: Children from birth to 18 years
description: Free health screening of children for birth defects, diseases, deficiencies and developmental delays.
benefits: Free screening and treatment (including surgery referral) at government facilities.
notes: Screening is done at Anganwadis and government schools by mobile health teams.
how_to_apply: Contact your Anganwadi, school or District Early Intervention Centre.

name: Universal Immunisation Programme (UIP)
target_group: Children and pregnant women
description: Free vaccines against serious diseases for children and pregnant women.
benefits: Free vaccination at government health centres and outreach camps.
notes: Follow the immunisation schedule on the Mother and Child Protection card.
how_to_apply: Visit your nearest Anganwadi, sub-centre or government hospital, or ask your ASHA worker.

name: PM National Dialysis Programme
target_group: Kidney patients needing dialysis, especially those below the poverty line
description: Free dialysis services at district hospitals.
benefits: Free dialysis for BPL patients at government facilities (details vary by state).
notes: Availability depends on dialysis centres in your district hospital.
how_to_apply: Contact the nephrology or dialysis unit at your district hospital.

name: Rashtriya Arogya Nidhi (RAN)
target_group: Poor patients with major life-threatening diseases
description: One-time financial help for treatment at government hospitals.
benefits: Financial assistance for treatment of major life-threatening diseases at government hospitals.
notes: Patients must be below the poverty line and treated at a government hospital. The hospital's Medical Superintendent forwards the application.
how_to_apply: Apply through the Medical Superintendent of the government hospital treating you.

name: Ni-kshay Poshan Yojana (TB Patients)
target_group: Tuberculosis patients on treatment
description: Cash support for nutrition while a patient is on TB treatment.
benefits: Monthly cash support (about ₹1,000) during the treatment period, paid directly to the bank account (verify current amount).
notes: The TB case must be notified on the Ni-kshay portal by a government or private provider.
how_to_apply: Ask your treating doctor or the nearest TB unit to register you on Ni-kshay.

name: e-Sanjeevani (Free Telemedicine)
target_group: Anyone who needs a doctor's consultation from home
description: A free online doctor consultation service run by the government.
benefits: Free video consultation and e-prescription from government doctors and specialists.
notes: Needs a smartphone or computer with internet access.
how_to_apply: Register on the e-Sanjeevani portal or app with your mobile number.

name: Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission (ABHA Health ID)
target_group: Any citizen
description: A free digital health ID that keeps your medical records in one place.
benefits: Free 14-digit ABHA number and digital health records that you can share with doctors.
notes: Creating an ABHA number is voluntary.
how_to_apply: Create your ABHA number on the ABDM portal or at a participating health facility.

name: Anganwadi Services (Saksham Anganwadi & Poshan 2.0)
target_group: Children under 6, pregnant and lactating women, and adolescent girls
description: Nutrition, early education and health services through Anganwadi Centres.
benefits: Supplementary nutrition, pre-school education, immunisation, health check-ups and referrals.
notes: Services are delivered through your local Anganwadi Centre.
how_to_apply: Register at your nearest Anganwadi Centre.

name: ADIP Scheme (Aids and Assistive Devices)
ministry: Dept. of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
target_group: Persons with disabilities needing assistive devices
description: Free or subsidised aids and appliances for persons with disabilities.
benefits: Wheelchairs, hearing aids, artificial limbs, tricycles and other devices, free or at a subsidy.
notes: Needs a disability certificate (40% or more) and a monthly income limit applies, so check the current limit. Distribution is often through camps.
how_to_apply: Contact your district disability office, an ALIMCO centre or watch for ADIP camps.

name: Unique Disability ID (UDID / Swavlamban Card)
ministry: Dept. of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities
target_group: Persons with disabilities
description: A single national ID and certificate for persons with disabilities.
benefits: One card accepted for pensions, scholarships, travel concessions and job reservation.
notes: Issued after a medical assessment by a certifying authority.
how_to_apply: Apply on the Swavlamban portal and complete the medical assessment.

name: Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme
target_group: Persons with severe disability aged 18–79 from BPL households
description: A monthly pension for persons with severe disabilities from poor households.
benefits: Monthly disability pension (central amount, often topped up by the state).
notes: Needs severe disability (80% or more) and a BPL household. Pension amounts vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Gram Panchayat, municipality or state social welfare department.

name: Rashtriya Vayoshri Yojana
target_group: Senior citizens aged 60+ from low-income households
description: Free physical aids for senior citizens with age-related disabilities.
benefits: Free aids such as walking sticks, hearing aids, spectacles, dentures and wheelchairs.
notes: For BPL seniors or those with low monthly income (check the current limit). Distribution is through camps.
how_to_apply: Register at a Vayoshri camp or through the district social welfare office.

name: National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS)
target_group: BPL families who lose their primary breadwinner (aged 18–59)
description: A one-time payment to support a poor family after the death of the main earner.
benefits: One-time assistance of ₹20,000 to the bereaved family.
notes: The deceased must have been the primary breadwinner aged 18 to 59 in a BPL household.
how_to_apply: Apply through your Gram Panchayat, municipality or state social welfare department.

name: One Stop Centre (Sakhi) and Women Helpline 181
target_group: Women facing violence or distress
description: Support under one roof for women affected by violence.
benefits: Free medical aid, police assistance, legal counselling, psychological support and temporary shelter.
notes: Call the Women Helpline 181, or 112 in an emergency.
documents: No documents are needed to seek help
how_to_apply: Call 181 or visit the nearest One Stop Centre.

name: Lakhpati Didi Initiative
target_group: Women members of self-help groups
description: Helps self-help group women earn a sustainable income of ₹1 lakh or more a year.
benefits: Skill training, bank credit and market linkage to build a stable livelihood.
notes: Delivered through DAY-NRLM self-help groups.
how_to_apply: Join or contact your local self-help group, or your block livelihood mission office.

name: Namo Drone Didi
target_group: Women self-help groups in rural areas
description: Provides drones to women self-help groups to rent to farmers for spraying and crop services.
benefits: Subsidy of about 80% on the drone (up to ₹8 lakh), plus training for pilot and technician (verify current terms).
notes: Groups are selected through DAY-NRLM and cluster federations.
how_to_apply: Contact your cluster-level federation or block livelihood mission office.

name: e-Shram Card (Unorganised Workers)
target_group: Unorganised-sector workers aged 16–59
description: A national database and card for unorganised workers to access welfare schemes.
benefits: Free e-Shram card with a Universal Account Number and ₹2 lakh accident insurance for the first year.
notes: Not for members of EPFO, ESIC or NPS, and not for income-tax payers.
how_to_apply: Register on the e-Shram portal or at a Common Service Centre.

name: Employees' State Insurance (ESIC)
target_group: Employees in covered establishments with limited wages
description: Health and social security insurance for workers and their families.
benefits: Medical care for you and your family, plus sickness, maternity and disablement cash benefits.
notes: Usually covers employees earning up to ₹21,000 per month in establishments with 10 or more workers (verify). Your employer registers you.
how_to_apply: Ask your employer to register you, or check the ESIC portal.

name: PM Viksit Bharat Rozgar Yojana (Employment Linked Incentive)
target_group: First-time employees registered with EPFO
description: An incentive for young people entering the formal workforce for the first time.
benefits: One month's wage incentive of up to ₹15,000 for first-time employees, paid in instalments (verify the current rules).
notes: For first-time EPFO-registered employees earning up to a wage ceiling, within the scheme's notified period. This is a newer scheme, so check the latest guidelines.
how_to_apply: Your employer registers you with EPFO, and the incentive is paid through the EPFO system.

name: National Career Service (NCS) Portal
target_group: Job seekers and students
description: A free national portal for job search, career counselling and job fairs.
benefits: Free job matching, career guidance, skill courses and access to job fairs.
notes: Free for job seekers.
how_to_apply: Register on the NCS portal.

name: Construction Workers Welfare Schemes (BOCW Welfare Boards)
ministry: Ministry of Labour & Employment / State Welfare Boards
target_group: Registered building and construction workers aged 18–60
description: Welfare benefits for construction workers through state welfare boards.
benefits: Education aid for children, medical and maternity help, accident and death benefits, and tool kit or pension support (varies by state).
notes: Usually needs proof of 90 days of construction work in the last year, and registration with your state welfare board.
how_to_apply: Register at your state construction workers' welfare board or labour office.

name: Credit Guarantee Scheme for Micro & Small Enterprises (CGTMSE)
target_group: Micro and small enterprises
description: A government guarantee that lets banks lend to small businesses without collateral.
benefits: Collateral-free business loans backed by a credit guarantee (limits are set by the current scheme rules).
notes: Applied for through your bank when you request a business loan.
how_to_apply: Ask your bank or lender for a loan under the CGTMSE guarantee.

name: Udyam Registration (MSME)
target_group: Micro, small and medium business owners
description: Free online registration that gives your business an official MSME identity.
benefits: A permanent MSME ID that helps with easier bank loans, subsidies and priority-sector benefits.
notes: Registration is free and based on self-declaration.
how_to_apply: Register on the Udyam Registration portal.

name: Kisan Vikas Patra (KVP)
target_group: Any adult resident
description: A post office savings certificate where your money grows to double over a fixed period.
benefits: Fixed return where the investment doubles in a government-set period (about 115 months at the current rate; verify).
notes: Interest rate is revised by the government every quarter.
how_to_apply: Buy at any post office.

name: National Savings Certificate (NSC)
target_group: Any resident individual
description: A 5-year savings certificate with government-set interest.
benefits: Fixed return over 5 years with a tax deduction under Section 80C (old tax regime).
notes: Interest rate is revised every quarter.
how_to_apply: Buy at any post office.

name: Post Office Monthly Income Scheme (POMIS)
target_group: Anyone wanting a regular monthly income from savings
description: A lump-sum deposit that pays you a fixed monthly income.
benefits: Fixed monthly income at a government-set interest rate over a 5-year term.
notes: Deposit limits apply for single and joint accounts. Check the current limits and rate.
how_to_apply: Open an account at any post office.

name: National Pension System (NPS)
target_group: Indian citizens aged 18–70
description: A voluntary retirement savings scheme with a pension after retirement.
benefits: Market-linked retirement savings with tax benefits and an annuity pension at retirement.
notes: A minimum yearly contribution applies. Rules on withdrawal and annuity are set by PFRDA.
how_to_apply: Open an account through a bank, post office or the eNPS portal.

name: NPS Vatsalya (for Children)
target_group: Parents or guardians of children under 18
description: A long-term retirement savings account that parents can open for a child.
benefits: Long-term market-linked savings for the child, which converts to a regular NPS account at 18.
notes: The account is in the minor's name and managed by the parent or guardian. A minimum yearly contribution applies.
how_to_apply: Open through a bank, post office or the eNPS portal.

name: Jeevan Pramaan (Digital Life Certificate)
ministry: Ministry of Electronics & IT / Dept. of Pension
target_group: Government pensioners
description: Lets pensioners submit their life certificate online without visiting the pension office.
benefits: Submit a life certificate using Aadhaar and biometrics from home, so pension continues without delay.
notes: For central, state and other government pensioners.
how_to_apply: Use the Jeevan Pramaan app or portal, or visit a Common Service Centre or bank branch.

name: e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)
target_group: Farmers and traders selling agricultural produce
description: An online trading platform that connects mandis across India.
benefits: Sell produce online to buyers in many mandis for better prices and payment directly to your bank account.
notes: Available only in mandis integrated with e-NAM.
how_to_apply: Register on the e-NAM portal or at your nearest e-NAM mandi.

name: Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (Organic Farming)
target_group: Farmers who adopt organic farming in clusters
description: Support for farmers to adopt organic farming.
benefits: Assistance of about ₹50,000 per hectare over three years for inputs, certification and marketing, with part paid directly to farmers (verify).
notes: Farmers form clusters of around 20 hectares. Support varies by state.
how_to_apply: Contact your state agriculture department or district agriculture office.

name: PM Krishi Sinchayee Yojana – Per Drop More Crop
target_group: Farmers adopting micro-irrigation
description: Subsidy to install drip and sprinkler irrigation systems and save water.
benefits: Subsidy on micro-irrigation (generally 55% for small and marginal farmers and 45% for others; verify).
notes: Subsidy rates and process vary by state.
how_to_apply: Apply through your state horticulture or agriculture department portal.

name: Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM)
target_group: Farmers and custom hiring centres
description: Subsidy on farm machinery to reduce labour and improve productivity.
benefits: Subsidy on tractors and implements, typically 40–50% depending on category (varies by state).
notes: Rates and eligible machines depend on your state.
how_to_apply: Apply on your state agriculture mechanization portal or through the district agriculture office.

name: Jal Jeevan Mission (Har Ghar Jal)
target_group: Rural households
description: Provides a tap water connection to every rural household.
benefits: A functional household tap connection with a regular supply of safe drinking water.
notes: Implemented village by village through the Gram Panchayat and Village Water Committee.
how_to_apply: Contact your Gram Panchayat or the Village Water and Sanitation Committee.

name: DAY-NULM (Urban Livelihoods Mission)
target_group: Urban poor households
description: Skill training, self-employment support and shelters for the urban poor.
benefits: Skill training with placement, interest-subsidised loans for self-employment and shelters for the homeless.
notes: Implemented through Urban Local Bodies.
how_to_apply: Contact your municipal office or Urban Local Body NULM cell.

name: PM-JANMAN (Development of Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups)
target_group: Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Group (PVTG) households
description: Basic facilities and services for the most vulnerable tribal communities.
benefits: Pucca houses, roads, drinking water, electricity, health, education and skill support in PVTG habitations.
notes: Only for notified PVTG communities in identified habitations.
how_to_apply: Contact your district tribal welfare office or Gram Panchayat.

name: DigiLocker
target_group: Any citizen
description: A free digital locker for storing and sharing official documents.
benefits: Authentic digital copies of Aadhaar, driving licence, marksheets and more, legally valid as originals.
notes: Requires an Aadhaar-linked mobile number.
how_to_apply: Sign up on the DigiLocker app or website.

name: One Nation One Ration Card (ONORC)
ministry: Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food & Public Distribution
target_group: Ration card holders, especially migrant workers
description: Lets you collect your ration from any fair price shop in India.
benefits: Use your existing ration card with Aadhaar biometrics to get foodgrains anywhere in the country.
notes: Requires an existing NFSA ration card linked to Aadhaar.
how_to_apply: Visit any fair price shop with your Aadhaar. You can also use the Mera Ration app.

name: Jan Shikshan Sansthan (JSS)
target_group: Non-literate, neo-literate and school-dropout youth and adults
description: Low-cost vocational training in local areas, especially for women and disadvantaged groups.
benefits: Low-cost skill courses such as tailoring, beauty, electrical and computer skills, with certification.
notes: Priority is given to women, SC/ST, minorities and rural communities. Age limits may differ by course.
how_to_apply: Contact the JSS centre in your district.

name: MY Bharat (Mera Yuva Bharat)
target_group: Young people aged 15–29
description: A national platform for youth volunteering, internships, skilling and leadership programmes.
benefits: Free access to volunteering, internships, events, skill courses and leadership programmes.
notes: Registration is free.
how_to_apply: Register on the MY Bharat portal.

name: HIMAYAT (Skill Training and Placement for J&K Youth)
target_group: Youth of Jammu & Kashmir and Ladakh aged 15–35
description: Free skill training linked to job placement for youth in J&K and Ladakh.
benefits: Free placement-linked skill training and job support.
notes: Training is run through approved partners. Check the current status and eligible trades.
how_to_apply: Contact an approved HIMAYAT training centre or your district skill office.

name: UMEED – J&K Rural Livelihood Mission
target_group: Rural households in Jammu & Kashmir, especially women
description: J&K's rural livelihood mission that builds self-help groups and income opportunities.
benefits: Self-help group formation, training, revolving fund and bank credit linkage.
notes: Run by the J&K UT government with central support under DAY-NRLM.
how_to_apply: Contact your block office or local self-help group under UMEED.

name: Ayushman Bharat SEHAT (Jammu & Kashmir)
ministry: J&K Health Department / National Health Authority
target_group: Residents of Jammu & Kashmir
description: Health insurance cover for J&K residents through the Ayushman Bharat framework.
benefits: Cashless health cover of up to ₹5 lakh per family per year at empanelled hospitals.
notes: Check current enrolment steps and required documents with the State Health Agency.
how_to_apply: Enrol at a Common Service Centre or empanelled hospital in J&K.
